fact_sheet.business_description: Delphi Corporation is a manufacturer of automotive components and systems currently operating under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection [D01]. The company maintains significant engineering relationships and customer programs, with General Motors serving as a critical customer and counterparty in its ongoing restructuring [D01].

final.memo:
Delphi Corporation is currently navigating a complex Chapter 11 restructuring while maintaining critical operations for General Motors, its primary customer [D01, D03]. The market has largely abandoned the company, fixating on liquidity burn and the perceived risks associated with GM's own financial instability [D05, D06]. This sentiment has created an opportunity to acquire senior debt tranches at a discount that fails to account for the structural protections of the bankruptcy process [D03, D04].

While operating margins have faced significant pressure, dropping to -21.1% in Q1 2009, the reorganization is not an exercise in equity valuation but a recovery play on debt [D03, D06]. With first-priority DIP loans of approximately $541 million and a substantial second-priority tier, the enterprise value—supported by the necessity of Delphi's automotive components—should provide meaningful coverage [D04]. We are focused on the recovery waterfall as the company emerges from this restructuring [D04].

Market participants are currently pricing in a worst-case scenario regarding Delphi’s reliance on GM [D05]. We believe this ignores the strategic necessity of Delphi's assets to its customers and the firm grip of the court-supervised proceedings [D01, D03]. Our analysis suggests that the risk of liquidation is overstated, and the focus should remain on the priority of the debt tranches within the reorganization plan [D04, D07].

The immediate path forward is defined by the final financing hearing scheduled for June 16, 2009 [D03, D07]. Our primary ask is the successful approval of the proposed $250 million incremental GM-subordinated DIP financing, which would provide the liquidity runway required to finalize the restructuring [D03, D04]. We will monitor the court filings closely and engage with the creditor committee should any terms deviate from the current expectation of preserving our priority status [D04, D07].

Risks remain high, particularly concerning the stability of GM as a counterparty and the inherent volatility of distressed assets [D01, D05]. A failure to secure the June financing would be an immediate trigger to reevaluate our position [D03, D07]. Our downside is protected by the priority of the DIP debt in the court-ordered waterfall [D04].

We are initiating a 3% position in Delphi's debt, sized to reflect our conviction in the court-supervised process despite the high-risk environment [D05]. We will hedge the broader automotive sector risk via index-level credit default swaps to ensure our exposure remains focused on the idiosyncratic recovery of this credit [D05, D08].
